source.title: Summary Factual Inconsistency Detection Based on LLMs Enhanced by Universal Information Extraction

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream factual-inconsistency detection accuracy for two Qwen2.5 model sizes, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss or fitting scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that detection accuracy generally aligns with scaling laws and that larger models perform better. The relevant results are balanced-accuracy scores for Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B. The cited Kaplan et al. findings are background, not results from this study. The paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, test extrapolation, or find a compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper on factual-inconsistency detection (UIEFID). It cites Kaplan et al. only to describe its Table 1 results: "aligns with the scaling laws". The only within-family size contrast is two off-the-shelf models, Qwen2.5-7B and 14B, on one downstream task. There is no scale sweep, no fitted curve and no link to pretraining loss, so the results cannot show whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale (V6). Two points can show only that the larger model scored higher. The paper does not test any version; the finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the emphasis is misplaced. The authors' main conclusion is that UIEFID improves the accuracy, efficiency and explainability of factual-inconsistency detection on AGGREFACT. The remark that accuracy "aligns with the scaling laws" is a passing interpretation of Table 1, not a tested conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates downstream factual-inconsistency detection accuracy across model sizes; it does not reproduce the original pretraining-loss scaling measurements or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with the evaluated strategy (zero-shot, fine-tuning, or fine-tuning plus UIEFID); the paper also reports variation across summary-compression-ratio clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen2.5-14B outscores Qwen2.5-7B in balanced accuracy on AGGREFACT under all three strategies. Zero-shot: 65.2 vs 59.5. Fine-tuned: 65.6 vs 61.1. Fine-tuned plus UIEFID: 79.8 vs 71.3. The 14B model also leads the other fine-tuned models across compression-ratio clusters in Figure 4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one model family, the larger model is a better factual-inconsistency detector. This is a two-point ordering on a single downstream task, not a scaling trend.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics, ACL 2025
record.problems: The scale comparison uses only two Qwen2.5 sizes and downstream balanced accuracy, not pretraining loss or a fitted predictive curve. The average scores aggregate across benchmark partitions, and the main Table 1 size-comparison results report no uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results left out. Other model and strategy scores in Table 1 do not provide an additional within-family size comparison for the reported 7B-versus-14B relationship.

untested.parts: Pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute: not measured.
Extrapolation from small-run fits: not done.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count: not studied.
Other modalities or regimes: no scaling fits. Fine-tuning is used, but not as a function of scale or data.
Predictability of downstream performance with scale or loss. Only two sizes, no fitted trend, no loss.

missing.what: Figure 4 accuracy by summary compression ratio for the four fine-tuned models with UIEFID, where Qwen2.5-14B is best. No rows record it; it is relevant only to the fits_no_version ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation "tests"/T2 and its V6 labels are dropped. The size contrast is incidental: two off-the-shelf models, one benchmark, no uncertainty in Table 1. That cannot address predictability. The Llama3 vs Llama3.1 comparison is not a size contrast. DeepSeek-R1 differs in architecture and training, so it cannot serve as a scale point.

Whether small-run power-law fits predict much larger runs.

Power laws in other modalities or training regimes.
The study compares only Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B for this size comparison; it does not relate performance to pretraining loss or fit a predictive scaling curve.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices, and bending of fitted scaling curves.

relation.reason: Section 3.3.1 interprets higher accuracy with more parameters as alignment with scaling laws, citing Kaplan et al.; it does not test a stated claim version.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates UIEFID detection performance. Its two within-family model sizes do not establish predictable scaling, and it neither fits nor uses a scaling law.

source_check.notes: The six rows represent three mirrored comparisons of the same two model sizes. Their reported AVG values establish a directional size association, without testing downstream predictability; appendix instructions are experimental prompt templates.
